hook_text: A king who lived on a hilltop, high above his people. Why up there?
clip_script: Mapungubwe Hill, about 1220 AD. A flat-topped sandstone hill with steep cliffs. The king moves up from K2 and lives on top, with stone walls marking the royal area. Ordinary people live in the valley below. The king is a sacred leader, believed to be close to the ancestors and able to bring rain. He controls trade, gives out wealth and rules over chiefs. One king, many people, a large area: the first state in southern Africa.
visual_style: Whiteboard sandstone hill with steep sides, stone walls drawing themselves on top, small huts in the valley below.
mood: Grand and respectful, like approaching a royal court.
pacing: Slow climb up the hill, a pause at the top, then clear facts about the king.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw Mapungubwe Hill with the royal area on top and the town below.
